reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows precipitation hardening in a Ti-based alloy, not a high-entropy alloy, and links it to improved corrosion resistance, but does not address room-temperature creep or homogeneous nanoscale precipitation in HEAs. E2 discusses creep resistance in HEAs but only in relation to Al addition and phase transformation, not aging-induced precipitation. Thus, the key premises about the specific mechanism and simultaneous improvements in HEAs lack direct prior support.
premises: Aging heat treatment can induce homogeneous nanoscale precipitation in high-entropy alloys
Nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding, reducing room-temperature creep
Nanoscale precipitates contribute to a more robust, passivating surface film that improves corrosion resistance
The treatment will simultaneously improve mechanical durability, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance relative to an untreated baseline
